facts.raw_span: a 5-day history of headache, nausea, and vomiting
Physical examination and laboratory tests were within normal limits
diagnosed with tension headache and sinusitis
vomiting persisted twice daily
developed ataxia, diplopia, and recurrence of her headache
T2-weighted MRI of the head showed increased signaling of the left temporal lobe, bilateral pontine regions, left peridentate nucleus, and cervical spinal cord
elevated opening pressure
blood pressure rose to 190/90 mmHg
serum sodium was 123 mEq/L
glucose 176 mg/dL
white-cell count 12,800 cells/mL
decreased sensorium, hallucinations, diminished attention span, and gait disturbance

concepts.why: The patient presented with headache, nausea, vomiting, ataxia, and diplopia, and the T2-weighted MRI showed increased signaling of the left temporal lobe, bilateral pontine regions, left peridentate nucleus, and cervical spinal cord, consistent with an acute demyelinating process.
The patient's symptoms and MRI findings are consistent with a demyelinating disease, and multiple sclerosis is a possible diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms and MRI findings are consistent with a demyelinating disease, and neuromyelitis optica is a possible diagnosis.
The patient's MRI findings showed progressive enlargement of the bilateral pontine regions with hydrocephalus and mass effect on the fourth ventricle, consistent with a brainstem glioma.
The patient presented with vomiting, ataxia, and decreased sensorium, and the lumbar puncture showed an elevated opening pressure, consistent with encephalitis.
The patient presented with vomiting, ataxia, and decreased sensorium, and the lumbar puncture showed an elevated opening pressure, consistent with toxic encephalopathy.
The patient's symptoms and MRI findings are consistent with a demyelinating disease, and acute disseminated encephalomyelitis is a possible diagnosis.
The patient's MRI findings showed progressive enlargement of the bilateral pontine regions with hydrocephalus and mass effect on the fourth ventricle, consistent with a low-grade glioma.

rationales.F05: Development of ataxia, diplopia, and recurrence of headache suggests a progressive neurological condition, increasing the likelihood of Acute Demyelinating Encephalomyelitis and Brainstem Glioma.
rationales.F06: T2-weighted MRI findings of increased signaling in the left temporal lobe, bilateral pontine regions, left peridentate nucleus, and cervical spinal cord are highly suggestive of an acute demyelinating process, supporting the diagnosis of Acute Demyelinating Encephalomyelitis and increasing the likelihood of Brainstem Glioma and Low-Grade Glioma.
rationales.F11: Elevated white-cell count may indicate an infectious or inflammatory process, increasing the likelihood of Encephalitis.
rationales.F12: Decreased sensorium, hallucinations, diminished attention span, and gait disturbance are indicative of a severe neurological condition, increasing the likelihood of Acute Demyelinating Encephalomyelitis, Encephalitis, and Toxic Encephalopathy.
